cards.explanation: The answer is that Abner is furious. "Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation." That's the text, friends, no guessing needed (2 Samuel 3:8). Ish-bosheth, Saul's son and the king Abner set up (2 Samuel 2:8-9), questioned the wrong man. I think he expected a quiet "yes, sire" and got a volcano instead.

The answer is False. Abner tells Ish-bosheth, "I have not delivered you into the hand of David…" (2 Samuel 3:8). He says he has been loyal to Saul's house, to his brothers and to his friends. Then he asks why he's accused of wrongdoing over this woman anyway.

The answer is throne. Abner says he'll "…establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba." (2 Samuel 3:10). That's a big promise from the man who set up Saul's son as king (2 Samuel 2:8-9). He also says it's what "…the LORD has sworn…" to David (2 Samuel 3:9). I think he knew exactly what he was saying.

The answer is True. The text says, "…for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him." (2 Samuel 3:11). One speech and the king goes silent. You know that moment when someone is so angry that you just stop talking? I think that was Ish-bosheth.

The answer is a covenant. Abner says, "Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you." (2 Samuel 3:12). A covenant is a solemn agreement between two sides. He's offering his help and asking for David's agreement in return.

The answer is Saul's daughter Michal. David says, "Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me." (2 Samuel 3:13). Michal is David's wife, and he later says so plainly to Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 3:14). No Michal, no meeting. That's a short guest list.

The answer is False. Ish-bosheth doesn't refuse. The text says, "…Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish." (2 Samuel 3:15). David asked, and Ish-bosheth acted. Paltiel is the husband she was taken from.

The answer is False, it's not David. Abner is the one who speaks: "Go back." Then Paltiel "returned home" (2 Samuel 3:16). Paltiel had followed her weeping all the way to Bahurim before that. I think that one hurts, so it's okay to feel it.

The answer is that the LORD will save Israel from the Philistines and all their enemies. Abner quotes the LORD: "Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies." (2 Samuel 3:18). He uses it to tell the elders to act now. Notice the words "…My servant David…" That's how the LORD names him.

The answer is the Benjamites. The text says, "Abner also spoke to the Benjamites." (2 Samuel 3:19). Benjamin was Saul's own tribe (1 Samuel 9:1-2). Then Abner went to Hebron to tell David what seemed good to Israel and the whole house of Benjamin. He was working the room, friends, one tribe at a time.

The answer is True. The text says, "…David held a feast for them." (2 Samuel 3:20). Abner showed up from the other side of the war with twenty men, and David set the table. That's a warm welcome. I'd have been checking for the exits, friends.

The answer is peace. The text says, "So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace." (2 Samuel 3:21). Abner had just promised to gather all Israel to David. David had held a feast for him and his men (2 Samuel 3:20), and then he left in peace. That's a good way to end a visit.
